active_family: joint IV+factor panel quality audit with factor-level reconstruction
current_bottleneck: Raw 571 joint checkpoints are not risk-manager acceptable. The cleaner factor framing is to generate factor returns/diffs and reconstruct factor levels deterministically from the last observed level, but the joint path still inherits IV-law weaknesses: weak long-horizon conditionality and uneven per-cell IV jump scale.
last_result_summary: 572 ran the official IV 11-suite on 571a h30: 3/11 with conditionality 1.8%, cross-cell correlation ratio 0.152, and pathwise max-jump KS 0.579. New joint audits rejected raw 571 h30 and h90 because factor level marginals/move scales failed. Deterministic factor-level reconstruction fixed move-scale failures but not all level marginals. The older full 537a checkpoint plus reconstruction is the best current joint candidate: factor checks, IV lower coverage, surface validity, IV-factor co-movement, and IV cross-cell structure pass, but IV conditionality and per-cell pathwise realism still fail.
next_step_recommendation: Do not deploy raw 571. For a reviewable joint stress prototype, use 537a with factor levels reconstructed from generated returns/diffs and clearly label it as a prototype. For a stronger deployable path, either combine the stronger 510a/568a IV stress deck with reconstructed factor overlays, or train a native joint model that models factor increments only and does not ask the network to independently generate duplicate factor levels.
current_best_note: 510a remains the best base learned IV law at 8/11. 564a/568a/570a remains the constrained IV stress-deck prototype. 537a plus deterministic factor-level reconstruction is now the best joint-factor prototype, but it is not a validated replacement because IV conditionality and per-cell pathwise realism still fail.
oracle_feasibility_note: 435a reaches 11/11 only as a validation-future oracle upper bound; it is not a deployable or learned conditional scenario generator.
